MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JULY 1, 2024

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Romanelli, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Repp-Loadsman, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JUNE 3, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  PUBLIC HEARING

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240141; ADDRESS: 759 SILVER SPUR ROAD,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: MOSTAFA RAHIMI;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240140) to operate a
  medical office use and a Precise Plan of Design (PPD-240142) for exterior improvements
  to an existing commercial building.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that Planning Application No. PA-240141 is
continued to a date uncertain in order to provide the applicant sufficient time to submit items that
are deficient from the application.

CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  TO CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 240141 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 1, 2024
  1
 AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES:
ABSENT: REPP-LOADSMAN, YOO
ABSTAIN:

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240194; ADDRESS: 449 SILVER SPUR ROAD,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: HOWARD FEIN; DESCRIPTION:
  A request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240195) for a medical office use
  (dermatology) located in an existing office building.

Senior Planner Berry presented Planning Application No. PA-240194 summarizing the staff
report. The applicant proposes to operate a medical office, specifically a dermatology practice.
The existing commercial general mixed-use overlay allows medical office with a conditional use
permit. The applicant currently operates a dermatology practice PV Dermatology Associates at
the Promenade Mall at 550 Deep Valley Drive in Suite 283 which offers a variety of medical,
surgical and cosmetic dermatology services The applicants practice has five employees and
operates Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the leasable area of this building is 4575 square feet and requires
a minimum of 23 parking spaces, which this site currently has. Staff has determined that due to
the low scale operation of the business, which is appointment-based services and the number of
employees, there should be no adverse impacts to the existing parking and circulation at the site.
Senior Planner Naughton further stated that the criteria to obtain a Conditional Use Permit have
been met.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution
No. PA-240194 approving the project and in accordance with the California Environmental Quality
Act, determine that the project is categorically exempt under Class 1, Section 15301.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the location of the proposed 90-unit complex and
this site. Senior Planner Berry stated that the two-acre property sits adjacent and immediately
behind towards the Peninsula Center.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that Dr.
Fein’s current practice located at The Promenade PV is operating under the property’s Master
Conditional Use Permit for medical office use.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired if the practice is being relocated or expanding. Director
Naughton stated that the practice is being relocated and explained that entitlements such as this
Conditional Use Permit, run with the land.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

There were no comments from the public.

VICE CHAIR OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-240194 APPROVING THE PROJECT AND IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT,
  DETERMINE THAT THE PROJECT IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT UNDER CLASS 1,
  SECTION 15301.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES:
ABSENT: REPP-LOADSMAN, YOO
ABSTAIN:

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 1, 2024
  2
 Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-
240194, a request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240195) for a medical office use
(dermatology) located in an existing office building at 449 Silver Spur Road. There is a 20-day
appeal period by which any member of the public or the City Council by their own motion may
appeal this project.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240163; ADDRESS: 710A DEEP VALLEY DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: SHANELLE SABINO;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240162) for a banquet room
  use located in an existing commercial building.

Senior Planner Berry presented Planning Application No. PA-240163 summarizing the staff
report. The applicant proposes to operate a banquet room venue that can be reserved for private
events, which requires a CUP in the Commercial General Mixed-Use (CGMU) district. The
property is currently zoned as commercial general mixed-use overlay, which does not mention
banquet rooms. However, it is proposed to be rezoned as part of the city's comprehensive zoning
update and the new CGMU zoning district does specifically list banquet room uses.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the proposed venue would be rented out for small-scale events.
Clients will make reservations for their event and provide their own food and beverage to their
private guests. The applicant plans to make the venue available for booking every day of the week
between the hours of 9:00 AM and midnight. The applicant has no immediate plans for additional
staff members. The main seating area for this unit is approximately 650 square feet, and the
minimum required parking spaces for the proposed use would be 31 spaces. Additionally, the
property shares a total of 221 spaces with contiguous properties through a shared use parking
agreement. Staff has determined that the proposed banquet room use would not cause adverse
impacts to the existing parking and circulation at the site.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the banquet room may have private gatherings that include live
music and/or amplified sound that would be located entirely indoors; although no noise impacts
are anticipated from this use, the banquet room is subject to the noise standards of RHEMC
Chapter 8.32. Measures will need to be taken to mitigate noise levels should they exceed those
limits and staff has proposed a condition of approval to that effect for this project.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the use is conditionally permitted in the zoning district pending
approval of the City’s Comprehensive Zoning Update. The use may not be effectuated until the
City Council conducts their second reading and adoption.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing and adopt Resolution
No. PA-240163.

VICE CHAIR OLSON asked about the adjoining businesses and their hours of operation. Senior
Planner Berry stated that the business to the south is Inkindle and they are by appointment only;
the business to the north is 710 Hair Studio and their hours are Tuesday through Sunday from
9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. and closed on Sunday.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if there is rear access to the unit. Senior Planner Berry stated
that there is access on the rear of the unit; however, there are stairs.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Senior Planner Berry stated that the
parking agreement is signed by the property owner and is for the benefit of the lessee.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton confirmed
that notices were sent to all the property owners who are party to the parking agreement.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that there is scheduled use for a specific parcel in the
parking agreement and asked if there would be any conflict. Director Naughton stated that the
church has specific provisions for use of the lot during weekend hours, but there should be no
conflict.

COMMISSION SCHACHTER asked if there will be a limit to how many people can attend an
event. Director Naughton stated that the space is limited in occupancy by the building code. If
there are complaints, and it is found that they exceed the permitted occupancy, it would be a
violation of the building code and the CUP. The maximum occupancy for this unit is 49.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that
there is no reciprocal agreement between the library and this property.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 1, 2024
  3
 CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that this property is across from the proposed 90-unit residential project
and expressed his concern with the noise level and traffic impacts.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

Shanelle Sabino, Applicant, thanked everyone, and for taking the time to review her application.
She stated that she looked into the church’s hours and stated that she is willing to change her
business hours in order to accommodate the parking concerns. She stated that she is also willing
to lower the number of people who can attend events; they will be signing a contract which will
include stipulating the maximum number of occupants.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Ms. Sabino stated that most events
will take place on the weekends, and she will be present during all events.

CHAIR MEDAWAR requested clarification on food, chairs and table being brought into the event
since it is an empty space. Ms. Sabino stated that food will be brought inb tables and chairs will
be provided.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Ms. Sabino stated that loading will
be done from the front of the unit since there are stairs in the rear access to the unit.

VICE CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern with alcohol being served on the site. Ms. Sabino
stated that she will investigate providing security for events that are serving alcohol.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about provisions for serving alcohol. Director Naughton
stated that this would go through ABC licensing and added that the owner’s contract should have
provisions to make sure that there is no conflict with ABC or City ordinances.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if loading could be done in the rear of the unit. Ms. Sabino
agreed.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the hours could be limited to 11:00 p.m. Ms. Sabino
agreed.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR to ordered.

CHAIR MEDAWAR expressed his concern with the location and the impact that this business
may have.

VICE CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern about alcohol and the noise. He stated that
monitoring of alcohol service and someone available to address noise complaints should be part
of the agreement.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is concerned with the alcohol and the 12:00 a.m.
hour.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that there are concerns and asked the applicant if she
would be willing to bring this back to the commission at a future date and provide further details
on how these concerns would be addressed.

Director Naughton stated that based on the concerns of the commission, the additional Conditions
of Approval are as follows: hours of operation limited to 11:00 p.m.; agreements between the
leaseholder and the lessee have conditions for obtaining ABC licenses; active monitoring of each
event; and loading and unloading in the rear of the tenant space only. Director Naughton stated
if the commission wishes to move forward, these conditions of approval can be part of the motion.
Additionally, this item could be brought back to the commission within 6 months to a year for
review, once the business has had time to operate.

CHAIR MEDAWAR expressed his concern approving this at this time since the tenants may not
be aware of the business that is being proposed and its potential impact.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 1, 2024
  4
 VICE CHAIR OLSON suggested that the applicant obtain a letter of approval from the surrounding
tenants. COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that if the applicant is not able to obtain letters
from all the tenants, the applicant may still come back to the commission for consideration.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if weekday hours could be limited to 9:00 or 10:00 p.m.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON

  TO CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240163 TO THE PLANNING
  COMMISSION MEETING OF MONDAY, AUGUST 5 TO ALLOW THE APPLICANT TO
  ADDRESS THE CONCERNS DISCUSSED AND TO INCLUDE THESE IN THE REVISED
  BUSINESS PLAN.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES:
ABSENT: REPP-LOADSMAN, YOO
ABSTAIN:

D.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240158; ADDRESS: 550 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE,
  SUITE 127; APPLICANT: MULTIVERSE PLATFORMS, INC.; DESCRIPTION: A request
  for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240248) to allow the Rolling Hills Bowl and Bar to
  include 5,540 square feet of ancillary arcade use within the Promenade on the Peninsula.

Senior Planner Berry presented Planning Application No. PA-240158 summarizing the staff
report. On May 6, 2024, the Planning Commission approved a CUP for a bowling alley with an
ancillary restaurant use at this location. This property is being rezoned as part of the City’s
Comprehensive Zoning Code Update. It is currently Commercial General Mixed-Use Overlay and
arcades are prohibited; the property is being rezoned to Commercial General Mixed-Use (CGMU).
The applicants were made aware that they would need to re-submit for a new CUP for the arcade
under the new CGMU zoning. The effectuation of this use is contingent upon City Council approval
and adoption of the updated zoning ordinance, and effectuation of the new ordinance.

Senior Planner Berry stated that parking was evaluated, and staff have determined that the
parking will accommodate the added demand of this use. Noise was also evaluated, and the
bowling alley is required to meet certain acoustic targets, therefore there are no noise impacts
anticipated from this use. Senior Planner Berry stated that the CUP findings have been met.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution
No. PA-240248, approving the project, and in accordance with the California Environmental
Quality Act (Public Resources Code determine that the project is Categorically Exempt under
Class 1, Section 15301-Existing Facilities.

VICE CHAIR OLSON asked about if the ABC license is a condition of approval. Director Naughton
stated that the applicant will need to obtain a Type 41 license before they can operate if they will
be serving alcohol on the premises.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to:

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

Raman Walia, Applicant, thanked the Planning Commission and the City for the opportunity. He
stated that the arcade is an integral part of the business to have a complete offering and that the
community enjoys a complete experience. The arcade will have 40+ kids-oriented entertainment
interactive consoles.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked about the projected opening date. Mr. Walia stated that April
2025 is the projected opening date.

Krista Hu, Promenade PV, added that the concept is total family entertainment.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. CUP-240248

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER
NOES:

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 1, 2024
  5
 ABSENT: REPP-LOADSMAN, YOO
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. CUP-
240248, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
CUP to allow 5,540 square feet of ancillary arcade use within the Rolling Hills Bowl and Bar
located at 550 Deep Valley Drive, Suite 127, within the Promenade on the Peninsula. There is a
20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City Council by their own motion
may appeal this project.

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there will be a City Council meeting on July 23, 2024.
Director Naughton stated that all indications are that the City Council will be cancelling the July
23 meeting.

CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he was approached by Jeff Earle, owner of the Red Onion, that
the retaining wall behind his building is collapsing. He is aware that it is a private property;
however, this is a public safety issue and asked that someone from the City go out to the property
to provide direction. Director Naughton stated that one of the issues is that this is outside of the
City’s jurisdiction in the City of Rancho Palos Verdes. Staff has been asked to reach out to Rancho
Palos Verdes Code Enforcement staff address this with the private property owner.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton stated that the League of California Cities annual conference will be held on
October 16-18 at the Long Beach Convention Center; more information will be provided at the
next meeting.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 28, 2024 (BUDGET WORKSHOP)

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 28, 2024

The PLANNING COMMISSION RECEIVED AND FILED ITEMS 11A AND 11B.

Director Naughton stated that the introduction and first reading of the Zoning Code Update was
done at the June 25, 2024, City Council meeting. The second reading and adoption is scheduled
at the City Council meeting on July 9, 2024, which included modifications clarifying that projects
that submit applications according to State density bonus law are not subject to discretionary
Precise Plan of Design; only the projects that submit applications under the City’s bonus level
development program would be subject to a discretionary design review under the Precise Plan
of Design.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if the housing overlay was removed from Kelly’s Korner.
Director Naughton stated that it was not removed. Staff recommended implementation measures
in the City’s Conservation Element to update the Landmark Overlay Ordinance. Director
Naughton stated that removing the housing would not have done as much to address the
commissions concerns as strengthening the landmark overlay will.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated at the first look meeting for the proposed 90-unit project
on Deep Valley Drive, the City Council have guidance to allow for more retail square footage and
there was concern with the design of the building. He asked if the developer were to file through
the State’s density bonus law, would these recommendations be incorporated into the project.
Director Naughton stated that the project was filed as a State density bonus project. The complete
application has not been received, but they are not exempt from CEQA. They can apply for
concessions from the development standards, and they are not subject to a Precise Plan of
Design.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 8:28 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
